source.title: Towards Understanding the Overfitting Phenomenon of Deep Click-Through Rate Models
source.authors: Zhaorui Zhang; Xiang-Rong Sheng; Yujing Zhang; Biye Jiang; Shuguang Han; Hong-Bo Deng; Bo Zheng

record.tranche_reason: The study measures test AUC over training epochs and reports a sharp degradation at the start of the second epoch, rather than an epoch-wise fall-rise-fall curve.
record.gate_note: The study tests training-time behavior in deep CTR models. Its reported result is a one-epoch overfitting pattern, not double descent. It does not test test error against sample size or measure interpolation thresholds. Some plotted values are not numerically stated in the text.
record.test_reason: The study characterises a one-epoch overfitting pattern in deep CTR models (test AUC drops sharply at the start of epoch 2) and its factors. It never frames or tests double descent. Belkin et al. appears only in a bracketed list of overfitting studies. Its epoch curves run only about 10 epochs, with no label-noise or interpolation-threshold analysis. So the lack of a second descent cannot speak to the epoch-wise double descent claim (V2). The model-parameter sweeps (Fig. 5) vary embedding dimension, MLP width and depth without locating an interpolation threshold, and are read as per-epoch curves, not test error against size. The results fit no version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: deep CTR models show a sharp drop at the start of epoch 2, linked to Embedding+MLP structure, fast-converging optimizers and feature sparsity. The authors hypothesise that the MLP layers rapidly adapt to the embedding distribution of already-trained samples. They also find that parameter count, activation, batch size, weight decay and dropout have no clear effect.
record.recipe_differences: The study examines CTR models on industrial and public recommendation data using test AUC over epochs; it does not reproduce the original double-descent experiments or measure interpolation thresholds.
record.method_sensitivity: The one-epoch phenomenon varies with learning rate and feature sparsity; reducing sparsity or using an extremely small learning rate alleviates or eliminates it, with reported performance degradation.

fits_no_version.finding: Deep embedding+MLP CTR models show abrupt test AUC degradation at the start of the second epoch on production, Amazon book and Taobao data. LR does not show it. It is reduced by a tiny learning rate or lower feature sparsity, at a cost in AUC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: One-epoch overfitting: deep CTR models with sparse ID features overfit abruptly at the start of the second epoch, so one-epoch training is best.

fits_no_version.finding: Varying embedding dimension, MLP width (0.1x-10x) and depth (1-8 layers) does not change the one-epoch phenomenon (Fig. 5). No test-AUC-vs-size curve is reported.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Parameter count does not govern one-epoch overfitting in CTR models.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Information and Knowledge Management (CIKM ’22)
record.problems: The epoch curves are reported as plots without numerical values or uncertainty estimates. The study uses CTR AUC rather than test error and does not test the interpolation threshold or the fall-rise-fall curve.
record.rows_left_out: Figures 5, 7-9, and 11 include additional parameter, activation, batch-size, optimizer, regularization, and feature-compression settings. Their plotted curve values are not numerically stated; the text summarizes most as not changing or alleviating the one-epoch phenomenon. The mechanistic A-distance and parameter-update results (Figures 14-16) measure proposed explanatory quantities, not test performance over epochs.

untested.parts: No test error vs model size across an interpolation threshold. Fig. 5 size sweeps are shown only as per-epoch curves.
No long-horizon epoch curves, label-noise setting, or search for a second descent.
No capacity sweep across model classes.
Weight decay and dropout are tested only against the one-epoch drop, not a double-descent peak. No label-noise manipulation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T5' and the V2 'challenges' label are not justified. The study does not address double descent. Its short epoch horizon (4-10 epochs) cannot show the absence of a later second descent. No verdicts are given.

versions.untested_parts: Test error as model size crosses the size that just fits the training set; the study varies model parameters but does not test a model-wise fall-rise-fall curve.
The study tests test AUC over epochs in CTR models, not test error over epochs in the original settings or a fall-rise-fall curve.
No sweep over training sample count near an interpolation threshold.
No general double-descent test across model classes.
No single effective-complexity measure is proposed or tested as predicting peak locations across axes.
The study does not test whether label noise or variance drives a double-descent peak, whether peaks split, or whether optimally tuned regularization removes such a peak.
No re-counting of model complexity by effective parameters.

rows.subject: online CTR prediction model of Alibaba display advertising platform
rows.operation_detail: Trained across multiple epochs and measured test user-weighted AUC.
rows.note: The text says AUC drops dramatically at the beginning of the second epoch and at the beginning of later epochs; it does not describe a fall-rise-fall curve.
rows.check: About 4 epochs of production-model test AUC. This is one-epoch overfitting, not a measure of epoch-wise double descent. The window is too short and no interpolation or noise regime is identified, so 'absent' against V2 is not supportable.

rows.subject: three-layer DNN CTR model
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and testing AUC across ten epochs.
rows.note: The authors state that the one-epoch phenomenon remains with this simplified model.
rows.check: 10-epoch curve showing a sharp drop at epoch 2. It does not bear on V2's fall-rise-fall over long training.

rows.subject: deep CTR prediction model
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and testing AUC across epochs.
rows.note: The authors state that the one-epoch phenomenon occurs on this data set.
rows.check: Amazon book, about 6 epochs. One-epoch overfitting, not a double-descent measure.

rows.subject: deep CTR prediction model
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and testing AUC across epochs.
rows.note: The authors state that the one-epoch phenomenon occurs on this data set.
rows.check: Taobao, about 6 epochs. One-epoch overfitting, not a double-descent measure.

rows.subject: logistic regression (LR) model
rows.operation_detail: Measured training and testing AUC across epochs.
rows.note: The authors report slight overfitting but no one-epoch phenomenon for LR, including across additional parameter settings.
rows.check: LR control for the one-epoch phenomenon. It does not bear on V2.

rows.subject: deep CTR prediction model
rows.operation_detail: Compared epoch curves using Adam with different learning rates.
rows.note: The text says the phenomenon is less obvious with an extremely small learning rate, at the expense of model performance; it also identifies this setting as one where the phenomenon does not occur.
rows.check: The learning-rate effect is on the one-epoch drop, not on a double-descent peak.

rows.subject: deep CTR prediction model
rows.operation_detail: Reduced feature sparsity by filtering IDs and measured test AUC across epochs.
rows.note: The text says the phenomenon is alleviated as m decreases; it identifies filter m=1e-4 as a setting where the phenomenon does not occur. The authors also report performance degradation from reducing sparsity.
rows.check: The feature-sparsity filter effect is on the one-epoch drop, not on a double-descent peak.

rows.subject: deep CTR prediction model
rows.operation_detail: Trained without item ID and history item ID feature fields and measured test AUC across epochs.
rows.note: The authors state that the one-epoch phenomenon does not occur without these sparse fields, but performance is worse than with all features.
rows.check: Removing sparse ID fields removes the one-epoch drop. Unrelated to double descent.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Test AUC over epochs in the production, Amazon book, and Taobao CTR settings
reader_labels.reason: The reported curves show abrupt degradation at the start of the second epoch, not the claimed fall-rise-fall shape (R1-R4).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The sharp epochwise phenomenon is reduced or absent with an extremely small learning rate or reduced feature sparsity, with performance costs reported for these changes (R6-R8).
